article_title: A Meta-Analysis of the Effects of Classroom Management Strategies and Classroom Management Programs on Students’ Academic, Behavioral, Emotional, and Motivational Outcomes
citation: Korpershoek, H., Harms, T., de Boer, H., van Kuijk, M., & Doolaard, S. (2016). A Meta-Analysis of the Effects of Classroom Management Strategies and Classroom Management Programs on Students' Academic, Behavioral, Emotional, and Motivational Outcomes. Review of Educational Research, 86(3), 643-680. https://doi.org/10.3102/0034654315626799
title: Meta-analytic corpus of 54 random and nonrandom controlled classroom management intervention studies (2003–2013)
description: The evidence base of the meta-analysis is a corpus of controlled intervention studies of classroom management strategies and programs in primary education. The article states that "The analysis included 54 random and nonrandom controlled intervention studies published in the past decade (2003–2013)." Studies were coded for four strategy categories and outcomes spanning academic, behavioral, social-emotional, and motivational domains, yielding an average effect of g = 0.22 across outcomes.
requirements: Studies must be random or nonrandom controlled intervention studies of classroom management in primary education
constraints: Limited to studies published 2003–2013
target_learning_goals: academic, behavioral, social-emotional, and motivational outcomes
examples: The corpus underlies the pooled estimate of g = 0.22 and the moderator analyses of strategy focus

article_title: The effect of fine motor skills on handwriting legibility in preschool age children
citation: Seo S-M. (2018). The effect of fine motor skills on handwriting legibility in preschool age children. J. Phys. Ther. Sci. 30: 324–327. https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/
title: Korean alphabet writing assessment for handwriting legibility
description: A short-range copy assessment of handwriting legibility in which children look at a Korean alphabet letter in a top box and reproduce it in the box below, using New Ming-style font, size 32, in two-centimeter squares. "The score ranged from 0 to 24 points, 24 being the highest. The inter-rater reliability was r=0.95", and test-retest reliability at one week was r=0.65.
requirements: Administered to children screened as normally developed in growth, development, and visual perception
constraints: Assesses legibility via copying Korean alphabet letters only; the article reports test-retest reliability of r=0.65
examples: Used as the legibility outcome measure for all 52 participants in this study

article_title: Needed research in method.
citation: Clayton C. Kohl. (1911). Needed Research in Method. The Journal of Educational Psychology. https://www.google.com/search?q=%22Needed+Research+in+Method%22+Kohl
title: Kohl's four-class taxonomy of books on method
description: The article organizes the method literature into a four-part classification: works on general method that emphasize the psychology of the learning process, works that summarize principles and apply them across a curriculum, works on special method by subject, and experimental studies emerging from the psychological laboratory. As the article states, "Books on method may be roughly divided into four classes." The taxonomy frames the paper's critical survey and its argument for a new research program in method.
requirements: A body of method literature to classify by emphasis: general psychology, applied principles, subject-specific method, or laboratory experiment
constraints: The article presents the division as rough, not exhaustive
target_learning_goals: understanding the organization of the literature on teaching method

article_title: Preliminary study of the effect of dental treatment upon the physical and mental efficiency of school children.
citation: Emma Kohnky, M.A. (1913). Preliminary Study of the Effect of Dental Treatment upon the Physical and Mental Efficiency of School Children. The Journal of Educational Psychology. https://www.jstor.org/journal/jeducpsych
title: Kohnky 1913 two-class dental-treatment comparison design with a Whipple test battery and coin-toss assignment
description: This element is the study design of Kohnky's 1913 preliminary study: two fifth-grade classes in one down-town school, matched on grading, neighborhood, and foreign-birth composition, with the experimental class chosen "decided by the toss of a coin." The treated class received full dental care including "treatment, tooth-brush drills, dinners," while a nurse and social visitor monitored compliance. Outcome measures were Whipple's tapping, cancellation, memory-span, and substitution tests plus weight and height, administered in October and May by two experimenters. The untreated class "received only such attention as they sought, which was found to be practically none."
requirements: Tests must be given by the same experimenters at both testing occasions, as the article arranged
A non-treated comparison class must be available in the same school with like home and social conditions
constraints: The author concedes the ongoing dental work itself introduced "the disturbing factor introduced by the actual carrying on of the dental work in the experimental class"
Only children present at both testings were counted
Results use medians rather than averages to neutralize extremes
target_learning_goals: physical and mental efficiency of school children
examples: Room 21 received dental treatment while Room 18 served as the comparison class; Room 21 was chosen experimentally by the toss of a coin
key_sources: Emma Kohnky, M.A. (1913). Preliminary Study of the Effect of Dental Treatment upon the Physical and Mental Efficiency of School Children. The Journal of Educational Psychology. https://www.jstor.org/journal/jeducpsych

article_title: Automated Data-Driven Generation of Personalized Pedagogical Interventions in Intelligent Tutoring Systems
citation: Kochmar, E., Vu, D. D., Belfer, R., Gupta, V., Serban, I. V., & Pineau, J. (2022). Automated Data-Driven Generation of Personalized Pedagogical Interventions in Intelligent Tutoring Systems. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education, 32, 323–349. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-021-00267-x
title: Korbit dialogue-based intelligent tutoring system
description: Korbit is "a large-scale, open-domain, dialogue-based ITS" using machine learning, NLP and reinforcement learning to provide interactive, personalized online learning, with around 20,000 students enrolled in data science, machine learning, and AI courses. It alternates short lecture videos with interactive exercises; an NLP-driven module verifies free-text solutions against reference solutions, and an inner-loop selects among interventions (hints, explanations, elaborations, mathematical hints, concept tree diagrams, multiple-choice quiz answers) via an ensemble of models based on the student's learning profile and last attempt.
requirements: Questions, reference solutions, and certain intervention types are created manually by course designers; data-driven content creation is future work
constraints: The 2020 experiments concern the machine learning and data science courses only
target_learners: online learners enrolled for free, mostly aged 18–35, globally distributed
target_learning_goals: machine learning and data science skills such as classification and regression analysis
examples: In the 2020 pilot, students received automatically generated hints and Wikipedia-based explanations during interactive exercises

article_title: Virtual or blended laboratories for healthcare students education: a systematized review.
citation: Safaeipour Ruhollah, Aalaa Maryam, Mojtahedzadeh Rita, Mohammadi Aeen, Asadzandi Shadi, Mousavi Atekeh. (2025). Virtual or blended laboratories for healthcare students education: a systematized review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07937-7
title: Kolb's Experiential Learning Theory and Cognitive Load Theory as explanatory accounts of video-based virtual laboratory effectiveness
description: The review attributes the effectiveness of audiovisual virtual laboratories to two established learning theories. Kolb's Experiential Learning Theory "explains how virtual labs enable reflective observation and conceptual understanding without any hands-on experiences." Cognitive Load Theory suggests that "well-designed educational videos allow learners to have control on the pace and focus on key information, improving comprehension and retention, so unnecessary mental effort decreased." Together these theories clarify how video-based virtual labs work in online learning environments.
requirements: Well-designed educational videos that let learners control pace and focus on key information
target_learners: Healthcare students learning via video-based virtual laboratories
target_learning_goals: Conceptual understanding and comprehension of laboratory content through video-based virtual labs

article_title: What is known about the development of relational competence in the mental health education of healthcare professionals - a scoping review.
citation: Beyene Lise Saestad, Vikman Miriam Dubland, Fugleberg Bruaset Geir Tarje, Hem Marit Helene, Andersen Elisabeth, Hammervold Unn Elisabeth. (2025). What is known about the development of relational competence in the mental health education of healthcare professionals – a scoping review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-08353-7
title: Kolb's experiential learning model as a framework for developing relational competence
description: The review uses Kolb's learning model as its explanatory framework for how relational competence develops. Learning is described as connecting new knowledge with existing understanding, either by "adding knowledge to existing understanding (assimilative learning) or by restructuring established understanding (accommodative learning)". Because relational competence involves personal change, the authors argue pedagogical methods must be linked to accommodative learning, with raising awareness, critical thinking, and reflection as central concepts. The learner moves between actor and observer roles through "concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualisation, and active experimentation".
requirements: Pedagogical methods for developing relational competence must be linked to accommodative learning, since the competence involves personal changes
target_learners: Students enrolled in health and social care education programs whose learning involves mental health-related topics
target_learning_goals: Development of relational competence for therapeutic relationships with persons with mental health challenges
key_sources: Beyene Lise Saestad, Vikman Miriam Dubland, Fugleberg Bruaset Geir Tarje, Hem Marit Helene, Andersen Elisabeth, Hammervold Unn Elisabeth. (2025). article_title: Exploring experiential learning within interprofessional practice education initiatives for pre-licensure healthcare students: a scoping review.
citation: Nagel Daniel A., Penner Jamie L., Halas Gayle, Philip Mark T., Cooke Carol A. (2024). Exploring experiential learning within interprofessional practice education initiatives for pre-licensure healthcare students: a scoping review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05114-w
title: Kolb's experiential learning theory (KELT) and its four-mode experiential learning cycle
description: KELT describes the role experience plays in the learning process as a dynamic, holistic, multi-dimensional approach to human development, developed by Kolb from the works of Dewey, Lewin, and Piaget. Kolb defines learning as "the process whereby knowledge is created through the transformation of experience", resulting from grasping and transforming experience through a cyclical sequence of stages. The review uses KELT as the anchor framework for mapping EL in IPP education, noting its four-mode recursive cycle of concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualization, and active experimentation.
requirements: Learning is viewed as continuous and grounded in experience rather than as an outcome
Learners progress through the four modes of the experiential learning cycle
constraints: The review found only eight included articles used an EL-specific theory or model, two based specifically on KELT
examples: The Leicester Model of Interprofessional Education incorporates elements of KELT with a 4-step education cycle for teaching interprofessional groups of students

article_title: The effect of experiential learning interventions on physical activity outcomes in children: A systematic review.
citation: Varman Sumantla D., Jones Rachel A., Kelly Bridget, Hammersley Megan L., Parrish Anne-Maree, Stanley Rebecca, Cliff Dylan P. (2023). The effect of experiential learning interventions on physical activity outcomes in children: A systematic review. PLOS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0294987
title: Kolb's four-stage experiential learning model as the framework for physical activity interventions
description: The review frames experiential learning through David Kolb's four-stage model: "concrete experience", "reflective observation", "abstract conceptualization" and "active experimentation". Learners participate in hands-on activities, develop perspectives through reflection, identify the significance of the learning experience from which new behaviours emerge, and apply the new concept practically. Reflection is described as the key component enabling learners to relate knowledge and behaviour systematically. The review uses this model to characterise and categorise the interventions it synthesises.
requirements: Interventions must incorporate an experiential learning activity in which children play a central role, physically do something, and have some autonomy to be creative, problem-solve or be reflective
constraints: The review restricted included studies to randomised controlled trials, a post hoc protocol deviation deemed the most robust level of evidence

article_title: Effects of Experiential Learning Approach on Students' Mathematical Creativity among Secondary School Students of Kericho East Sub-County, Kenya
citation: Chesimet M. C, Githua B.N, Ng’eno, J. K. (2016). Effects of Experiential Learning Approach on Students’ Mathematical Creativity among Secondary School Students of Kericho East Sub-County, Kenya. Journal of Education and Practice, 7(23). http://www.iiste.org
title: Kolb's four-stage experiential learning cycle
description: The article adopts Kolb's experiential learning model, in which "the process of learning is divided into four stages all of which must be gone through for learning to be most effective": concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualization and active experimentation. The learner has an experience, reflects on it from several perspectives, forms concepts or theories from the reflections, and tests them in new situations, which become new concrete experiences. The article uses this cycle as the theoretical basis for the ELA treatment condition.
requirements: All four stages must be gone through for learning to be most effective, as the article states
examples: The ELA treatment taught Statistics I through the four-stage cycle, with the teacher describing activities during concrete experience and promoting acceptance of diverse thinking during reflective observation

article_title: Effectiveness of Experiential Learning-Based Teaching Material in Mathematics
citation: Mutmainah, Rukayah, Mintasih Indriayu. (2019). Effectiveness of experiential learning-based teaching material in Mathematics. International Journal of Evaluation and Research in Education (IJERE), Vol. 8, No. 1, March 2019, pp. 57-63. http://iaescore.com/journals/index.php/IJERE
title: Kolb's experiential learning theory: knowledge created through transformation of experience via four stages
description: The article grounds its teaching material in Kolb's experiential learning theory, which "defines learning as the process whereby knowledge is created through the transformation of experience". The material operationalizes this as four stages: "Concrete Experience (CE), Reflection Observation (RO), Abstract Conceptualization (AC), and Active Experimentation (AE)", aiming to make students experience, observe, think, and act. Concrete experience uses picture illustrations; reflection asks students to consider various points of view; conceptualization integrates observations into comprehension; and implementation applies material to solve problems.
requirements: Students must be actively involved in experiencing, observing, thinking, and acting during the learning process rather than only listening to lectures or reading material
constraints: The article applies the theory to fifth-grade elementary Mathematics content, specifically the volume of cube and beam
target_learning_goals: Mathematics concept comprehension and cognitive ability
examples: The developed teaching material displays picture illustrations suited to the material, then guides students through reflection, conceptualization, and application stages

article_title: The Effect of the Layered Curriculum on the 6th Grade Students' Learning Styles in Science Lesson
citation: Koc Akran, S., & Uzum, B. (2018). The effect of the layered curriculum on the 6th grade students' learning styles in Science lesson. International Journal of Educational Methodology, 4(3), 141-152. https://doi.org/10.12973/ijem.4.3.141
title: Kolb's experiential learning style model with four styles (converging, diverging, assimilating, accommodating)
description: According to Kolb's model, individuals' learning styles lie in a cycle of four modes: "Concrete Experience, (RO) Reflective Observation, (AC) (Abstract Conceptualization), and (AE) Active Experience". Each individual's style emerges from a combination of these forms, yielding four styles: converging (AC+AE), diverging (CE+RO), assimilating (AC+RO) and accommodating (CE+AE). The Learning Styles Inventory, a 12-item scale with four ranked options per item, is used to determine which style fits an individual; the Turkish translation by Askar and Akkoyunlu was used in this study.
requirements: Kolb's Learning Styles Inventory (12 items, four options each, ranked 1-4) to classify individuals
constraints: Learning style is not determined by a single mode but by the combination of the four forms
examples: The study classified 43 students into the four styles via the Turkish Kolb inventory and analyzed style distributions by gender with chi-square

article_title: The Effect of Mobile Learning on Students' Achievement and Conversational Skills
citation: Abdellah Ibrahim Mohammed Elfeky & Thouqan Saleem Yakoub Masadeh. (2016). The Effect of Mobile Learning on Students' Achievement and Conversational Skills. International Journal of Higher Education, Vol. 5, No. 3. https://doi.org/10.5430/ijhe.v5n3p20
title: Koole's FRAME model as the framework for the mobile learning intervention
description: The study grounded its mobile learning design in Koole's (2009) Frame Model for Mobile Education, which the article describes as "dependent upon Situational, Realistic, Contextual Learning, and Social Constructivism." The model comprises three circles — Device Aspect (physical/technical characteristics of devices), Learner Aspect (emotional aspects and motivation), and Social Aspect (interactions and cooperation) — and three intersections: Device Usability (DL), Social Technology (DS), and Interactive Learning (LS), which accounts for theories of learning and teaching.
requirements: Mobile applications must align with the device, learner, and social aspects and their intersections
constraints: Applied in this study to a Blackboard-based site for Android and IOS devices
target_learners: University students using mobile devices for coursework
examples: The researchers mapped Blackboard forums, groups, and blogs to the Social Aspect and Social Technology intersection.

article_title: Outdoor Experiential Environmental Education: An Adult-Centred Intervention for the Affective Domain
citation: Okur-Berberoglu, E. (2017). Outdoor experimental environmental education: An adult-centred intervention for the affective domain. International Electronic Journal of Environmental Education, 7(1), 34-58. https://www.iejee.com
title: Kolb's experiential learning theory as a design framework for developing the affective domain
description: The article uses Kolb's experiential learning theory as the design basis for both indoor and outdoor programmes, treating learning as a cycle in which "knowledge gets constructed and reconstructed in this cyclical process". Its four stages are concrete experience (experiencing), reflective observation (reflecting), abstract conceptualisation (thinking) and active experiment (doing). The researcher personally carried out the concrete experience and reflective observation stages with all groups, and used the theory because Kolb holds that learning is not only cognitive but also affective, including thinking, feeling, perceiving and behaving.
requirements: Programme activities must be designed in accordance with Kolb's experiential learning cycle, with concrete experience and reflective observation stages carried out for participants
constraints: The active experiment stage was left out of control group 2's programme because its methodology followed a different type of active learning
target_learning_goals: development of affective-domain concepts such as interest, anxiety, curiosity and motivation in environmental education
examples: Participants viewed disturbing YouTube footage (Canadian seal slaughter, Chernobyl, BP Deepwater Horizon) as concrete experience, followed by reflective discussion; 19 doctoral-level lecturers delivered the abstract conceptualisation stage on 19 environmental subjects

article_title: Acquisition of Language and Intercultural Competences in Tourism and Hospitality Studies through Active Experimentation in Second Life
citation: Mercedes Rico García and Paula Ferreira da Silva. (2017). Acquisition of Language and Intercultural Competences in Tourism and Hospitality Studies through Active Experimentation in Second Life. Teaching English with Technology, 18(2), 69-92. http://www.tewtjournal.org
title: Kolb's experiential learning cycle as a four-step instructional sequence culminating in virtual-world active experimentation
description: The study organizes instruction as Kolb's (1984) experiential learning cycle: "learning is seen as a process where learners (1) are exposed to specific experiences, (2) observe and reflect on those situations, (3) create abstract concepts, and (4) test learning in future learning or professional situations". Phase 1 delivers steps 1-3 in class through multimedia input, comparison and reflection; Phase 2 is the fourth step, active experimentation, carried out as professional simulations either in Second Life (experimental) or in class (control). The authors state this cyclical methodology "can be applied to a gre at number of interactions in SL".
requirements: Instruction must sequence experience, observation/reflection and abstract conceptualization before the active-experimentation step
constraints: Evaluated in a monocultural, monolingual Spanish hospitality setting with B1+/B2 English-level students
target_learners: third-year undergraduate tourism and hospitality students
examples: Phase 1 used videos, games, film trailers and photographs; Phase 2 used hotel front-desk, event-planning, tour-guiding and sustainable-tourism role-plays in SL or class

article_title: A Learning Style Comparison between Synchronous Online and Face-to-Face Engineering Graphics Instruction
citation: Goodridge, W. H., Lawanto, O., & Santoso, H. B. (2017). A Learning Style Comparison between Synchronous Online and Face-to-Face Engineering Graphics Instruction. International Education Studies, 10(2). https://doi.org/10.5539/ies.v10n2p1
title: Kolb's Learning Style Inventory as a framework for categorizing learner styles in engineering education
description: The article adopts Kolb's Learning Style Inventory, "a valid model to measure and assess student learning styles," grounded in an Experiential Learning Model with four dialectic learning modes: concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualization, and active experimentation. The LSI categorizes learners as accommodating, diverging, assimilating, or converging, each a resultant of two learning modes. The authors used the 12-question LSI 3.1 to classify 108 engineering graphics students and analyze performance by style.
requirements: Administering the 12-question Kolb LSI 3.1 with students rating four answers per question on ranks of 1 to 4, with the two highest learning-mode scores determining the learning style
constraints: The article notes the Diverging learning style was not represented in the synchronous online group and was severely underrepresented in the face-to-face group
target_learning_goals: engineering graphics and solid modeling proficiency
examples: Students with scores CE (22), AE (19), AC (48), and RO (31) were categorized into Assimilating because AC and RO were the two highest scores

article_title: The Effect of Cooperative Learning Model and Kolb Learning Styles on Learning Result of the Basics of Politics
citation: Sugiharto. (2015). The Effect of Cooperative Learning Model and Kolb Learning Styles on Learning Result of The Basics of Politics. Journal of Education and Practice, Vol.6, No.21. http://www.iiste.org
title: Kolb learning styles (assimilator and accommodator) as a moderator of instructional-model effects
description: The article uses Kolb's experiential account of learning styles as a moderator variable in its 2x2 design. It states that "Kolb considered lear ning as a process where knowledge is created through the transformation of experience" and that style types "among other things are assimilator and accommodator". Assimilators combine thinking and observing, favouring lecture-style, structured, independent work; accommodators combine feeling and doing, favouring cooperative, experimental activity. The study treats style as relatively permanent habit in receiving and managing information.
requirements: Educators need knowledge of students' learning styles, obtained here by questionnaire, before assigning them to a matched learning model
constraints: The study limits the style construct to the assimilator and accommodator types and to cognitive-domain learning results in one course
target_learners: First-semester university students in a Faculty of Social Sciences
target_learning_goals: Cognitive-domain understanding of basic political science concepts
examples: Learning styles were measured by questionnaire and crossed with GI and STAD treatments in a 2x2 treatment-by-level design

article_title: Determining the Effects of Reflection Type and Cognitive Style on Students' Content Knowledge
citation: Blackburn, J. J., Robinson, J. S., & Kacal, A. (2015). Determining the effects of reflection type and cognitive style on students' content knowledge. Journal of Agricultural Education, 56(3), 195-209. https://doi.org/10.5032/jae.2015.03195
title: Kolb's Experiential Learning Theory (ELT) four-step cycle with reflection-in-action
description: Kolb's experiential learning theory describes a four-step process where experiences are transformed into learning opportunities: concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualization, and active experimentation. For learning to occur, learners must be guided through the full cycle, though where the cycle begins for each student should not be a concern for teachers. The study integrates Schön's (1983) distinction between reflection-on-action (occurring following an experience) and reflection-in-action (occurring continuously during an experience), positioning reflection as a critical stage for constructing knowledge from experience.
requirements: Learners must be guided through the full four-step experiential learning cycle for learning to occur
constraints: Where the cycle begins for each student should not be a concern for teachers, per Baker et al. (2014) and Kolb (1984)
target_learning_goals: science content knowledge through experiential learning
examples: The biofuels laboratory exercise served as the concrete experience, with verbal or written reflection-in-action embedded during the investigation

article_title: Bridging the gap in adrenal crisis management: a pilot simulation-based pre post educational intervention to improve resident knowledge.
citation: Resnick Ortal, Matalka Leen, Foster Christy. (2026). Bridging the gap in adrenal crisis management: a pilot simulation-based pre post educational intervention to improve resident knowledge. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09924-y
title: Kolb's Experiential Learning Theory as the framework for simulation with structured debriefing
description: The intervention was informed by Kolb's Experiential Learning Theory, in which "learners engage in a concrete clinical experience followed by reflective observation and abstract conceptualization during structured debriefing." The 45-minute simulation provided the concrete experience and the 15-minute advocacy-inquiry debriefing operationalized reflective observation and conceptualization. Educational outcomes were evaluated at Kirkpatrick's Level 2 (learning).
requirements: A structured debriefing phase following the concrete clinical experience
constraints: Outcomes measured only at Kirkpatrick Level 2; clinical behavior and patient outcomes not assessed
target_learning_goals: Adrenal crisis recognition and management knowledge
examples: The debriefing focused on four key domains: recognition and clinical decision-making, stress-dose glucocorticoid administration, electrolyte correction, and outpatient sick-day management

article_title: Hybrid simulation approach enhances technical and non-technical skills in therapeutic pharmacology education.
citation: Changuiti O, Mahou FZ, Decormeille G, Koraich N, El Hsaini H. (2026). Hybrid simulation approach enhances technical and non-technical skills in therapeutic pharmacology education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09983-1
title: Kolb's experiential learning cycle as an account for sequencing complementary simulation modalities
description: The article attributes the substantial gains observed in the study to the sequence of complementary learning modalities employed, consistent with Kolb's experiential learning cycle. The authors state that sequencing simulations where learning points from one session are integrated into the next while increasing the focus on professional realism is a key factor for success. title: Kolb's experiential learning cycle as the design framework for VP-case CPD
description: The article structures VP-case CPD around Kolb's four stages of experiential learning: "concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualization, and active experimentation". Working a VP case is the concrete experience; nurses reflect on the information presented; they conceptualize it; and they actively experiment by managing the case and searching resources. The authors use this cycle to explain why VP cases foster a deliberate learning process that improves clinical reasoning.
requirements: A VP case must let learners experience, observe and reflect on, conceptualize, and actively manage a realistic clinical scenario for the cycle to operate
constraints: The framework is applied to CPD for in-service nurses managing non-communicable diseases at primary health centers in Rwanda
target_learners: in-service nurses at primary health care centers
target_learning_goals: clinical reasoning for diagnosis and management of non-communicable diseases
examples: Participants managed hypertension, depression, prostate cancer, and gastric cancer VP cases in the Virtual Case System, then reviewed the feedback section after answering the case questions
